entries.title: Exodus 28:1
segments: The high-priest, among the Jews, was a striking type of the Messiah, who, as a priest, entered the holy place with his blood, and obtained eternal redemption for his people.

entries.title: Exodus 28:2
segments:
Holy garments; garments to be used not on ordinary occasions, but when engaged in the public worship of God. 
 
  For glory and for beauty; the glory and beauty of the priestly garments represented the holiness, purity, and dignity of their office; and, since their priesthood typified that of Christ, these holy and glorious garments prefigured the infinite dignity, excellence, and spiritual beauty of Jesus Christ our great High-priest.

entries.title: Exodus 28:3
segments: The ingenuity of men, their genius and judgment, their ability to plan, and their power to execute, all come from God, and should all be devoted to his service.

entries.title: Exodus 28:5
segments: Gold; that is, golden thread.  The manner of forming them is described

entries.title: Exodus 28:6
segments: The ephod; this, with the breastplate attached to it, was the outermost of the garments belonging to the high-priest.  The ephod was a short garment reaching down, according to the testimony of the ancients, to the middle of the thighs.  Originally it seems to have been without sleeves.  Each shoulder-piece consisted of two projections from the body of the ephod, the one coming up from before and the other from behind, and united on the shoulder at their extremities by an onyx-stone set in gold, which served also for a clasp.

entries.title: Exodus 28:8
segments: Shall be of the some, according to the work thereof; these words seem to mean, that it shall be woven as a part of the ephod; and be of the same materials and texture.

entries.title: Exodus 28:9
segments:
vv 9,12. 
 
Our great High-priest, of whom Aaron was a type, bears all his people upon his heart, presents their wants before his Father, and will save to the uttermost all who come unto God through him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.

entries.title: Exodus 28:11
segments:
Signet; a seal. 
 
  Ouches; sockets.

entries.title: Exodus 28:12
segments: For a memorial; to put them in remembrance that Aaron, as priest appeared in their behalf before the Lord.

entries.title: Exodus 28:14
segments: Two chains; these are generally thought to be the same chains mentioned
, their connection with the ephod being here considered, and there, their connection with the breastplate.

entries.title: Exodus 28:15
segments: Breastplate of judgment; so called because worn by the high-priest when he applied to the Lord for his judgment, or decision, in matters about which they inquired of him.

entries.title: Exodus 28:16
segments: Four square--being doubled; after being doubled over so as to form a sort of bag or pouch, it was four square: consequently the whole piece, before doubling, was two spans in length.  A span is half a cubit, that is, between nine and ten inches.

entries.title: Exodus 28:21
segments: The names of all his people are in the Lamb's book of life; he will never blot them out, but will acknowledge them as his redeemed people, before his Father and the holy angels.

entries.title: Exodus 28:22
segments: Chains at the ends; at the two upper corners on the outside were two rings of gold, to which these chains were attached,

entries.title: Exodus 28:25
segments: The two ouches; the two sockets of the onyx-stones on the shoulder- pieces of the ephod.

entries.title: Exodus 28:26
segments: Two rings of gold; on the two lower corners of the breastplate on the inside, corresponding to the two rings in the ephod,

entries.title: Exodus 28:27
segments: Two other rings of gold--ephod; this verse may be literally rendered thus: "And thou shalt make two rings of the ephod below, in its forepart, over against its coupling, above the girdle of the ephod."  The coupling is that of the shoulder pieces at the onyx-stones,

.  These rings are to be directly opposite to this coupling below.  The two upper corners of the breastplate being fastened to the onyx-stones by wreathed chains of gold, and the two lower corners to the rings here mentioned by a lace of blue, the breastplate is thus made firm over the heart,

; a beautiful and most expressive symbol of the unchangeable love which Christ, our great High-priest, bears toward his people, and in which all his earthly ministers should strive to imitate him.  It has been well said that Christ bears his people on his shoulders by his almighty power and efficacious atonement, and on his heart by his everlasting love.

entries.title: Exodus 28:30
segments:
Urim--Thummim; that is, lights and perfections: according to some, these were no other than the precious gems themselves, through which God, by a supernatural lustre, manifested his will; others think that they were precious stones placed in the pouch of the breastplate, and used in consulting God's will.  The whole subject is involved in obscurity. 
 
All spiritual illumination and perfection are in Jesus Christ, and he is able and willing to communicate according to the wants of all who feel their need, and heartily apply to him.

entries.title: Exodus 28:31
segments: Robe of the ephod; worn underneath the ephod.

entries.title: Exodus 28:32
segments: The hole of it; the hole through which the head passed when it was put on.

entries.title: Exodus 28:33
segments: Pomegranates; balls in the form of pomegranates, a species of fruit shaped like an apple.

entries.title: Exodus 28:34
segments: A golden bell and a pomegranate; one after the other, alternately, round the hem of the robe.  The bell was an emblem of pleasant sound, and the pomegranate of abundant fruitfulness; indicating the duty of makng a good profession, and abounding in fruits of holiness.

entries.title: Exodus 28:38
segments:
Bear the iniquity of the holy things; typically make atonement for their sins, and thus obtain forgiveness through the atonement of Christ. 
 
Holiness to the Lord was the great and all-pervading characteristic of the Redeemer; and it is his great design, by his word, his Spirit, and his providence, in all his dispensations to make his people like him.

entries.title: Exodus 28:41
segments:
Anoint them; in token of their dedication to the sacred office. 
 
  Sanctify them; set them apart, and devote them to their work.

entries.title: Exodus 28:43
segments: Bear not iniquity; do not commit sin, by neglecting divine directions, thus exposing themselves to divine judgments.
